title: Finite scalar extension inverts the actual quotient completion unit
statement: Fix l,E, an arbitrary scheme X, an arbitrary unbounded object K of the completed-coefficient ordinary derived category, and n≥0. The actual positive finite derived scalar extension at exponent n+1 [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] sends the actual IntegralOnSlice.completionUnit at K [def-pur-integral-derived-operations] to an isomorphism. No completeness, boundedness, constructibility or invertibility of l on X is assumed.

source.place: Maps-used sentence, primitive tensor/pullback coefficient comparison and open-factor normalization.

proof.text: Choose a good flat-term K-flat representative P using the localization qGood. Apply the already proved fromOrdinary helper of integralOperationRoos_effectivity directly to the ordinary IntegralOnSlice quotient tower of P, with its literal finite scalar extension complexes and identity finite restriction comparisons. This gives invertibility of the adjoint of each actual mapping-cocone projection; its proof already assembles the normalized coefficient sequence and applies normalized DVR Roos effectivity.

Compute roosUnit followed by mappingCocone.fst and the nth product projection. mappingCocone.lift_fst and Pi.lift_π identify this composite with the nth ordinary scalar-extension adjunction unit: the augmentation and that unit both send x to 1 tensor x, by their defining section formulas. The finiteModel_unit helper in the finite-mate comparison puts the normalized derived scalar unit in these same cochain coordinates, followed by coefficientFiniteReductionModel and exact scalar-restriction localization factors.

Left naturality and injectivity of the finite scalar adjunction Hom equivalence identify finite scalar extension of the Roos augmentation followed by the invertible projection adjoint with the K-flat finite reduction comparison, which is an isomorphism. Cancel the projection adjoint. The defining completionUnit equation on P then cancels completionComparison. Finally naturality along the representative isomorphism transports the result to K. This includes n=0 and zero or unbounded complexes and imposes no geometric characteristic condition.

proof_origin.place: Primitive quotient completion augmentation: reuse ordinary quotient tower effectivity, compute its actual projected unit, and cancel its finite adjoint. Lean proof follows the existing representative route without new obligations.

theorem finiteReduction_completionUnit (X : Scheme.{u})
    (K : DerivedCategory (scalarReductionSource l E X)) (n : ℕ) :
    IsIso ((coefficientFiniteDerivedExtension l E X n).map
      ((IntegralOnSlice.completionUnit l E X none).app K))
